53	@dataclass
54	class FileSizeGrowthSignal:
55	    """Positive if the target file has grown by >= min_bytes since the last call.
56	
57	    First call is always True (baselining). Absent file -> False.
58	    State lives on the instance so CompositeProbe can reuse it across cycles.
59	    """
60	
61	    path: str
62	    min_bytes: int
63	    _last_size: int | None = field(default=None, init=False, repr=False)
64	
65	    def evaluate(self) -> bool:
66	        target = Path(self.path)
67	        if not target.exists():
68	            self._last_size = None
69	            return False
70	
71	        current_size = target.stat().st_size
72	        if self._last_size is None:
73	            self._last_size = current_size
74	            return True
75	
76	        grew_by = current_size - self._last_size
77	        self._last_size = current_size
78	        return grew_by >= self.min_bytes

116	    """ANY-mode composition with failure threshold."""
117	
118	    signals: list[Signal]
119	    failure_threshold: int = 3
120	    period_s: int = 30
121	    initial_delay_s: int = 90
122	    _failure_count: int = 0
123	    _started_at: float | None = None
124	
125	    def evaluate_once(self) -> bool:
126	        """Return True if ANY signal reports alive."""
127	        return any(signal.evaluate() for signal in self.signals)

130	        """Advance or reset the failure counter."""
131	        if alive_this_cycle:

2	"""Safe post-task reaper for dispatch worktrees.
3	
4	Reaps the dispatch worktree bound to one task_id only after the task is terminal
5	and the worktree is clean.  Optional ACP runtime-review paths are reaped only
6	when the owning task is terminal, the path can be bound to that task, and no
7	live process holds the path.

9	Default mode is dry-run; pass --apply to delete anything.

27	_DISPATCH_WORKTREES_ROOT = ROOT / ".worktrees" / "dispatch"
28	_ACP_RUNTIME_ROOT = _DISPATCH_WORKTREES_ROOT / "acp"
29	
30	_ACTIVE_STATUSES = frozenset({"spawning", "running"})

35	        "timeout",

46	    "GIT_DIR",

141	    if proc.returncode != 0:
142	        return True
143	    resolved = path.resolve()
144	    entry_path: Path | None = None
145	    locked = False

147	        if line.startswith("worktree "):
148	            if entry_path == resolved:

151	            locked = False
152	        elif line.startswith("locked"):

163	    falls back to the git worktree lock bit as a conservative proxy.

167	            ["lsof", "+D", str(path)],
168	            capture_output=True,
169	            text=True,
170	            timeout=10,
171	            check=False,
172	        )
173	    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, subprocess.SubprocessError):
174	        return _git_worktree_is_locked(path, ROOT)
175	    if proc.returncode != 0:

198	def _find_acp_runtime_worktrees(task_id: str) -> list[Path]:
199	    """Find ACP runtime worktrees whose name binds them to task_id.
200	
201	    Actual ACP execution worktrees are named ``runtime-{label}-{uuid}``.  The
202	    skill text also references ``runtime-review-*`` prefixes; we include both
203	    shapes but never return paths by prefix alone -- the caller must still
204	    require task terminal status and a dead process before reaping.
205	    """
206	    root = _ACP_RUNTIME_ROOT
207	    if not root.is_dir():
208	        return []
209	    label = _safe_label(task_id)
210	    candidates: list[Path] = []
211	    for path in root.iterdir():
212	        if not path.is_dir():

214	        name = path.name
215	        if name.startswith(f"runtime-{label}-") or (name.startswith("runtime-review-") and label in name):

128	def _posix_norm(path: str) -> str:
129	    """Collapse // and . segments; leave .. rejection to the caller."""
130	    cleaned = path.replace("\\", "/")
131	    # posixpath.normpath keeps a leading /; for relative paths it collapses // and .
132	    return posixpath.normpath(cleaned)

135	def normalize_claim(raw: str) -> PathClaim:
136	    """Normalize a single --research-owned-path value into a claim."""
137	    text = (raw or "").strip().replace("\\", "/")
138	    if not text or text in {".", "./"}:
139	        return PathClaim(raw=raw, kind=ClaimKind.UNKNOWN, norm="")
140	
141	    # Preserve subtree intent before normpath (which strips trailing /).
142	    is_double_star = text.endswith("/**")
143	    is_subtree_slash = text.endswith("/") and not is_double_star
144	    body = text[: -len("/**")] if is_double_star else text.rstrip("/") if is_subtree_slash else text
145	
146	    # Any wildcard in the body (or non-/** wildcards) → unknown before norm.
147	    if any(ch in body for ch in "*?[") or ("*" in text and not is_double_star):
148	        return PathClaim(raw=raw, kind=ClaimKind.UNKNOWN, norm=text)
149	
150	    norm = _posix_norm(body)
151	    if norm in {"", "."}:
152	        return PathClaim(raw=raw, kind=ClaimKind.UNKNOWN, norm=text)
153	
154	    # Reject absolute / parent escapes / drive-qualified paths as unknown
155	    # (not comparable safely as repo-relative claims).
156	    drive_qualified = len(norm) >= 2 and norm[0].isalpha() and norm[1] == ":"
157	    if (
158	        norm.startswith("/")
159	        or norm.startswith("../")
160	        or norm == ".."
161	        or "/../" in f"/{norm}/"
162	        or drive_qualified
163	    ):
164	        return PathClaim(raw=raw, kind=ClaimKind.UNKNOWN, norm=text)
165	
166	    if is_double_star or is_subtree_slash:
167	        return PathClaim(raw=raw, kind=ClaimKind.SUBTREE, norm=norm)
168	
169	    return PathClaim(raw=raw, kind=ClaimKind.FILE, norm=norm)

172	_DISPLAY_LIMIT = 120
173	# Cc control, Cf format (bidi overrides, zero-width joiners), Cs surrogate,
174	# Co private use — none of these belong in a one-line operator message. Zl/Zp
175	# are U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR and U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR: not control
176	# characters by category, but terminals and log viewers render them as line
177	# breaks, so leaving them through kept the forged-line hole open (CF re-review
178	# of #5804, F001).
179	_UNSAFE_UNICODE_CATEGORIES = frozenset({"Cc", "Cf", "Cs", "Co", "Zl", "Zp"})
180	
181	
182	def sanitize_for_display(value: object, *, limit: int = _DISPLAY_LIMIT) -> str:
183	    """Make a ledger-sourced string safe to print in an operator message.
184	
185	    Task ids and claim paths come from other processes, so they reach this
186	    message as untrusted text. Raw interpolation let a task id containing a
187	    newline or an ANSI escape forge extra operator-looking lines in the guard's
188	    own output (CF review of #5804).
189	
190	    Escaping only the ASCII control range would still let U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT
191	    OVERRIDE visually reverse the rest of the line, so every Unicode
192	    control/format code point is escaped — as an escape sequence rather than a
193	    deletion, so the value stays recognisable — and the result is bounded.
194	    """
195	    units: list[str] = []
196	    for ch in str(value):
197	        if unicodedata.category(ch) in _UNSAFE_UNICODE_CATEGORIES:
198	            point = ord(ch)
199	            units.append(f"\\x{point:02x}" if point < 0x100 else f"\\u{point:04x}")
200	        else:
201	            units.append(ch)
202	
203	    if sum(len(u) for u in units) <= limit:
204	        return "".join(units)
205	
206	    # Truncate on escape-unit boundaries. Slicing the joined string could cut
207	    # "‮" into a bare backslash, which is both misleading and a different
208	    # string than the one that is actually blocking the operator (CF re-review
209	    # of #5804, F002). One character of the budget is reserved for the ellipsis.
210	    kept: list[str] = []
211	    used = 0
212	    for unit in units:
213	        if used + len(unit) > limit - 1:
214	            break
215	        kept.append(unit)
216	        used += len(unit)
217	    return "".join(kept) + "…"

226	    """Render one blocking peer as `task-id(pid N)` for operator-facing messages."""

232	def _dedupe_peers(rows: list[dict[str, object]]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
233	    """Collapse claim rows to distinct peers, preserving first-seen order.
234	
235	    A peer holding four claims is ONE blocking peer. Counting rows made the
236	    message say "(+1 more)" about a single agent (CF review of #5804).
237	    """
238	    seen: dict[tuple[str, object], dict[str, object]] = {}
239	    for row in rows:
240	        seen.setdefault(_peer_key(row), row)
241	    return list(seen.values())

244	def refusal_message(
245	    *,
246	    conflicts: list[dict[str, object]],
247	    unprovable_peers: list[dict[str, object]],
248	    self_unprovable: bool,
249	    unknown: list[PathClaim],
250	) -> str:
251	    """Explain a REFUSE so the operator can act on it.
252	
253	    Two very different conditions used to share the string "path ownership
254	    conflict": a real overlap between declared paths, and an *unprovable*
255	    admission where nobody overlaps but some active writer declared no paths at
256	    all. The second one reported ``conflicts=0`` while refusing, which reads as
257	    a guard bug and hides the fix (declare paths, or override deliberately).
258	    """
259	    if conflicts:
260	        # Group overlapping paths under the peer that holds them: N claim rows
261	        # from one agent is one blocker, not N blockers.
262	        by_peer: dict[tuple[str, object], list[str]] = {}
263	        labels: dict[tuple[str, object], str] = {}
264	        for row in conflicts:
265	            key = _peer_key(row)
266	            labels.setdefault(key, _peer_label(row))
267	            claim = row.get("other_claim") or {}
268	            norm = claim.get("norm", "?") if isinstance(claim, dict) else "?"
269	            paths = by_peer.setdefault(key, [])
270	            if norm not in paths:
271	                paths.append(str(norm))
272	        shown_keys = list(by_peer)[:3]
273	        shown = ", ".join(
274	            f"{labels[key]} on "
275	            + ", ".join(sanitize_for_display(p) for p in by_peer[key][:2])
276	            + (
277	                f" (+{len(by_peer[key]) - 2} more paths)"
278	                if len(by_peer[key]) > 2
279	                else ""
280	            )
281	            for key in shown_keys
282	        )
283	        more = f" (+{len(by_peer) - 3} more)" if len(by_peer) > 3 else ""
284	        return f"path ownership conflict (REFUSE): overlaps {shown}{more}"
285	
286	    parts: list[str] = []
287	    if self_unprovable:
288	        declared = (
289	            ", ".join(repr(sanitize_for_display(c.raw)) for c in unknown[:3])
290	            if unknown
291	            else "none declared"
292	        )
293	        parts.append(
294	            f"this task declared no comparable --research-owned-path ({declared})"
295	        )
296	    distinct_peers = _dedupe_peers(unprovable_peers)
297	    if distinct_peers:
298	        peers = ", ".join(_peer_label(p) for p in distinct_peers[:3])
299	        more = f" (+{len(distinct_peers) - 3} more)" if len(distinct_peers) > 3 else ""
300	        parts.append(f"active writer(s) with undeclared paths: {peers}{more}")
301	    detail = "; ".join(parts) or "no comparable claims among active writers"
302	    return (
303	        f"cannot prove write-path disjointness (REFUSE): {detail}. "
304	        "No actual path overlap was found. Fix by re-running the undeclared "
305	        "dispatches with --research-owned-path, or pass "
306	        "--allow-path-overlap '<why this is safe>'."
307	    )

310	def claims_conflict(a: PathClaim, b: PathClaim) -> bool:
311	    """Return True if two concrete claims intersect. UNKNOWN never proves overlap alone."""
312	    if a.kind == ClaimKind.UNKNOWN or b.kind == ClaimKind.UNKNOWN:
313	        return False
314	    if a.kind == ClaimKind.FILE and b.kind == ClaimKind.FILE:
315	        return a.norm == b.norm
316	    if a.kind == ClaimKind.FILE and b.kind == ClaimKind.SUBTREE:
317	        return a.norm == b.norm or a.norm.startswith(b.norm + "/")
318	    if a.kind == ClaimKind.SUBTREE and b.kind == ClaimKind.FILE:
319	        return b.norm == a.norm or b.norm.startswith(a.norm + "/")
320	    # subtree/subtree
321	    return (
322	        a.norm == b.norm
323	        or a.norm.startswith(b.norm + "/")
324	        or b.norm.startswith(a.norm + "/")
325	    )

328	def _pid_alive(pid: int) -> bool:
329	    if pid <= 0:
330	        return False
331	    try:
332	        os.kill(pid, 0)
333	    except ProcessLookupError:
334	        return False
335	    except PermissionError:
336	        return True
337	    else:
338	        return True

346	def _task_still_active(
347	    task_id: str,
348	    pid: int | None,
349	    state_dir: Path,
350	    *,
351	    created_at: float | None = None,
352	    now: float | None = None,
353	) -> bool:
354	    """True if the ownership claim should still be considered held.
355	
356	    Admission records the short-lived CLI PID first; the worker PID is patched
357	    in after Popen. Live-PID trust is therefore limited to
358	    ``ADMISSION_PID_GRACE_S`` so a recycled CLI PID cannot pin claims forever
359	    (Claude CF #5649 F001). Outside the grace window, task-state + worker PID
360	    are authoritative.
361	    """
362	    state_path = state_dir / f"{_safe_task_state_name(task_id)}.json"
363	    status = None
364	    state_pid: int | None = None
365	    if state_path.is_file():
366	        try:
367	            data = json.loads(state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
368	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
369	            data = {}
370	        if isinstance(data, dict):
371	            status = data.get("status")
372	            raw_pid = data.get("pid")
373	            if isinstance(raw_pid, int):
374	                state_pid = raw_pid
375	            elif isinstance(raw_pid, str) and raw_pid.isdigit():
376	                state_pid = int(raw_pid)
377	
378	    clock = time.time() if now is None else now
379	    in_grace = (
380	        created_at is not None and (clock - float(created_at)) <= ADMISSION_PID_GRACE_S
381	    )
382	
383	    # Within grace only: live ledger PID holds claim (admission→state-write race).
384	    if in_grace and pid is not None and pid > 0 and _pid_alive(pid):
385	        return True
386	
387	    if status in TERMINAL_TASK_STATUSES:
388	        return False
389	
390	    # Prefer state worker PID once present (long-lived).
391	    check_pid = state_pid if state_pid is not None else (pid if in_grace else None)
392	    if check_pid is not None and check_pid > 0 and not _pid_alive(check_pid):
393	        return False
394	    # No state file and no pid → treat as stale (cannot prove active).
395	    if status is None and (check_pid is None or check_pid <= 0):
396	        return False
397	    # spawning/running/needs_finalize/empty with live pid (or unknown pid) = active.
398	    # no_deliverable is terminal: there is no unfinished tree to protect.
399	    if status in ("running", "spawning", "needs_finalize", "", None):
400	        if check_pid is None or check_pid <= 0:
401	            # State says active but no pid — keep claim conservatively if status explicit.
402	            return status in ("running", "spawning", "needs_finalize")
403	        return _pid_alive(check_pid)
404	    return False

407	class OwnershipLedger:
408	    def __init__(
409	        self,
410	        path: Path | None = None,
411	        *,
412	        task_state_dir: Path | None = None,
413	        mode: GuardMode | None = None,
414	    ) -> None:
415	        self.path = Path(path) if path is not None else default_ledger_path()
416	        self.task_state_dir = (
417	            Path(task_state_dir) if task_state_dir is not None else default_task_state_dir()
418	        )
419	        # Default follows env (REFUSE after #5645 soak). Explicit mode still wins.
420	        self.mode = mode if mode is not None else env_guard_mode()
421	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

423	    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
424	        conn = sqlite3.connect(str(self.path), timeout=30.0, isolation_level=None)
425	        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
426	        conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
427	        conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000")
428	        conn.execute(
429	            """
430	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS write_claims (
431	                task_id TEXT NOT NULL,
432	                claim_json TEXT NOT NULL,
433	                pid INTEGER,
434	                created_at REAL NOT NULL,
435	                PRIMARY KEY (task_id, claim_json)
436	            )
437	            """
438	        )
439	        conn.execute(
440	            """
441	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS admission_events (
442	                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
443	                ts REAL NOT NULL,
444	                task_id TEXT NOT NULL,
445	                event TEXT NOT NULL,
446	                payload TEXT NOT NULL
447	            )
448	            """
449	        )
450	        return conn

452	    def _reconcile_stale(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> list[str]:
453	        released: list[str] = []
454	        rows = conn.execute(
455	            "SELECT task_id, pid, MIN(created_at) AS created_at "
456	            "FROM write_claims GROUP BY task_id, pid"
457	        ).fetchall()
458	        for row in rows:
459	            task_id = str(row["task_id"])
460	            pid = row["pid"]
461	            pid_i = int(pid) if pid is not None else None
462	            created = float(row["created_at"]) if row["created_at"] is not None else None
463	            if not _task_still_active(
464	                task_id, pid_i, self.task_state_dir, created_at=created
465	            ):
466	                conn.execute("DELETE FROM write_claims WHERE task_id = ?", (task_id,))
467	                released.append(task_id)
468	        return released

470	    def release(self, task_id: str) -> None:
471	        with self._connect() as conn:
472	            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
473	            conn.execute("DELETE FROM write_claims WHERE task_id = ?", (task_id,))
474	            conn.execute("COMMIT")

476	    def update_claim_pid(self, task_id: str, new_pid: int) -> None:
477	        """Patch ledger PID after the long-lived worker is spawned."""
478	        with self._connect() as conn:
479	            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
480	            conn.execute(
481	                "UPDATE write_claims SET pid = ? WHERE task_id = ?",
482	                (int(new_pid), task_id),
483	            )
484	            conn.execute("COMMIT")

486	    def admit(
487	        self,
488	        *,
489	        task_id: str,
490	        mode: str,
491	        owned_paths: Sequence[str] | None,
492	        allow_path_overlap: str | None = None,
493	        pid: int | None = None,
494	        caller: str = "delegate.cmd_dispatch",
495	    ) -> AdmissionResult:
496	        """Attempt admission. WARN always admits; REFUSE may refuse."""
497	        if mode not in WRITE_CAPABLE_MODES:
498	            return AdmissionResult(
499	                admitted=True,
500	                mode=self.mode,
501	                would_refuse=False,
502	                reason="read-only exempt",
503	                skipped=True,
504	            )
505	
506	        claims = [normalize_claim(p) for p in (owned_paths or ())]
507	        # Deduplicate by normalized ledger identity (kind+norm) so repeatable
508	        # CLI flags / equivalent spellings do not crash on PRIMARY KEY.
509	        seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
510	        deduped: list[PathClaim] = []
511	        for claim in claims:
512	            key = (claim.kind.value, claim.norm)
513	            if key in seen:
514	                continue
515	            seen.add(key)
516	            deduped.append(claim)
517	        claims = deduped
518	        unknown = [c for c in claims if c.kind == ClaimKind.UNKNOWN]
519	        concrete = [c for c in claims if c.kind != ClaimKind.UNKNOWN]
520	        # No declared paths still participate in the ledger when peers are active
521	        # (cannot prove disjointness — Fable solo-admit only when truly alone).
522	        no_claim_sentinel = PathClaim(
523	            raw="*", kind=ClaimKind.UNKNOWN, norm="*"
524	        )
525	
526	        with self._connect() as conn:
527	            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
528	            self._reconcile_stale(conn)
529	
530	            # Same-task_id live reservation: concurrent duplicate dispatch race
531	            # between admission and state write (CF r7 F001). Refuse if another
532	            # live PID already holds claims for this task_id.
533	            same_rows = conn.execute(
534	                "SELECT DISTINCT pid FROM write_claims WHERE task_id = ?",
535	                (task_id,),
536	            ).fetchall()
537	            for row in same_rows:
538	                other_pid = int(row["pid"]) if row["pid"] is not None else None
539	                if other_pid is None or other_pid <= 0:
540	                    continue
541	                if pid is not None and other_pid == pid:
542	                    continue  # same process re-admit / retry
543	                if _pid_alive(other_pid):

547	                        "caller": caller,
548	                    }
549	                    if self.mode == GuardMode.REFUSE:

551	                            "INSERT INTO admission_events (ts, task_id, event, payload) "

555	                                task_id,

557	                                json.dumps(event, sort_keys=True),
558	                            ),
559	                        )
560	                        conn.execute("COMMIT")

562	                            admitted=False,
563	                            mode=self.mode,
564	                            would_refuse=True,
565	                            reason=(
566	                                f"task_id already admitted by live pid={other_pid} (REFUSE)"
567	                            ),
568	                            conflicts=[
569	                                {
570	                                    "other_task_id": task_id,
571	                                    "other_pid": other_pid,
572	                                    "our_claim": {"raw": "(same-task race)"},
573	                                }
574	                            ],
575	                        )

579	                        "VALUES (?,?,?,?)",
580	                        (

582	                            task_id,

601	                            }

605	            active_rows = conn.execute(

607	                (task_id,),

609	            active: list[tuple[str, PathClaim, int | None]] = []

"""Hermetic tests for scripts.fleet.post_task_reap.

Tests exercise the hard guards without touching the real checkout:
- never reap while task status is spawning/running
- never reap a dirty worktree
- never reap without binding task state to a registered dispatch worktree
- never reap ACP runtime paths by name/substring; only ``acp_runtime_paths`` in
  task state authorizes reaping
- liveness probe failure is fail-closed (retain) for both main and ACP paths
- default dry-run; --apply required for deletion
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "scripts"))

from scripts.fleet import post_task_reap


def _safe_label(task_id: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "-", task_id).strip("-._")[:32]


@pytest.fixture
def hermetic_reap(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """Redirect post_task_reap to a fresh git repo and task directory."""
    repo_root = tmp_path / "repo"
    tasks_dir = tmp_path / "tasks"
    tasks_dir.mkdir(parents=True)

    monkeypatch.setattr(post_task_reap, "ROOT", repo_root)
    monkeypatch.setattr(post_task_reap, "_TASKS_DIR", tasks_dir)
    monkeypatch.setattr(post_task_reap, "_DISPATCH_WORKTREES_ROOT", repo_root / ".worktrees" / "dispatch")
    monkeypatch.setattr(post_task_reap, "_ACP_RUNTIME_ROOT", repo_root / ".worktrees" / "dispatch" / "acp")

    _init_repo(repo_root)

    # Tests control process liveness so we stay independent of lsof availability.
    monkeypatch.setattr(post_task_reap, "_probe_path_liveness", lambda _path: False)

    return repo_root, tasks_dir


def _run(args: list[str], cwd: Path, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(
        args,
        cwd=cwd,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=check,
    )


def _init_repo(repo_root: Path) -> None:
    repo_root.mkdir(parents=True)
    _run(["git", "init"], cwd=repo_root)
    _run(["git", "config", "user.email", "test@example.com"], cwd=repo_root)
    _run(["git", "config", "user.name", "Test User"], cwd=repo_root)
    (repo_root / "README.md").write_text("# test\n", encoding="utf-8")
    _run(["git", "add", "README.md"], cwd=repo_root)
    _run(["git", "commit", "-m", "initial"], cwd=repo_root)


def _add_dispatch_worktree(repo_root: Path, agent: str, task_id: str) -> Path:
    branch = f"{agent}/{task_id}"
    _run(["git", "branch", branch], cwd=repo_root)
    path = repo_root / ".worktrees" / "dispatch" / agent / task_id
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    _run(["git", "worktree", "add", str(path), branch], cwd=repo_root)
    return path


def _add_external_worktree(repo_root: Path, name: str) -> Path:
    branch = f"external/{name}"
    _run(["git", "branch", branch], cwd=repo_root)
    path = repo_root / ".worktrees" / name
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    _run(["git", "worktree", "add", str(path), branch], cwd=repo_root)
    return path


def _add_acp_runtime_worktree(repo_root: Path, task_id: str, locked: bool = False) -> Path:
    label = _safe_label(task_id)
    path = repo_root / ".worktrees" / "dispatch" / "acp" / f"runtime-{label}-deadbeef"
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    _run(
        ["git", "worktree", "add", "--detach", "--no-checkout", str(path), "HEAD"],
        cwd=repo_root,
    )
    if locked:
        _run(
            ["git", "worktree", "lock", "--reason", f"active ACP execution {label}", str(path)],
            cwd=repo_root,
        )
    return path


def _write_task_state(
    tasks_dir: Path,
    task_id: str,
    status: str,
    worktree_path: Path | None,
    *,
    agent: str = "kimi",
    acp_runtime_paths: list[Path] | None = None,
    pid: int | None = None,
) -> None:
    state: dict[str, Any] = {
        "task_id": task_id,
        "agent": agent,
        "status": status,
    }
    if worktree_path is not None:
        state["worktree_path"] = str(worktree_path)
    if acp_runtime_paths:
        state["acp_runtime_paths"] = [str(p) for p in acp_runtime_paths]
    if pid is not None:
        state["pid"] = pid
    safe = task_id.replace("/", "_").replace("\\", "_")
    (tasks_dir / f"{safe}.json").write_text(json.dumps(state), encoding="utf-8")


def test_no_task_state(hermetic_reap):
    repo_root, tasks_dir = hermetic_reap
    report = post_task_reap.post_task_reap("missing-task", tasks_dir=tasks_dir, repo_root=repo_root)

    assert report["task_status"] is None
    assert report["main_worktree"]["action"] == "retained"
    assert "no task state" in report["main_worktree"]["reason"]

    report = post_task_reap.post_task_reap("running-task", tasks_dir=tasks_dir, repo_root=repo_root)

    assert report["task_status"] == "running"
    assert report["main_worktree"]["action"] == "retained"
